title: SDK first-run experience: journey map + handoff templates (draft)
content:
Status: rough draft / brainstorming notes. Not client-facing.

Purpose:
- Define the "first-run" developer experience for the Redwood SDK (the very first 10 minutes after installing the package). Focus on minimizing time-to-value, setting up defaults that avoid common mistakes, and surfacing performance/cost tradeoffs.

Goals (measurable):
- New user completes a minimal generate call within 10 minutes.
- Telemetry event for 'first_success' fired in >60% of signups who install SDK.
- Reduce helpdesk tickets for 'auth errors' by 40% via clearer error messages and startup checks.

Primary audience:
- Software engineers integrating Redwood into user-facing web apps and internal tools.
- Secondary: ML engineers evaluating model variants.

Principles to follow:
- Opinionated defaults: choose safe token limits, retries, and timeouts for first-run.
- Fail fast, explain faster: provide actionable error text with remediation hints and links to docs.
- In-product guidance only — keep CLI/docs short; prefer example code and a one-file runnable demo.

Proposed 8-step first-run journey (developer POV):
1) Install + import: pip/npm install -> import redwood (or require).
2) Quick auth check: CLI helper or a short code snippet that runs `redwood.whoami()` and prints the configured account + region.
3) Minimal generate example: 3 lines to call generate and print output (uses small model shim for free tier).
4) Validate latency & cost hints: show estimated token cost and expected p50/p95 latency for the selected model.
5) Telemetry opt-in prompt (non-blocking): ask to opt into anonymous first-run metrics.
6) Run a short sample that demonstrates streaming + function calling (toggle).
7) Troubleshooting panel: common errors and CLI auto-fix suggestions (e.g., missing API key, rate limit).
8) Next steps CTA: link templates + sample apps by platform (Node, Python, React).

Minimal code example (Python) to ship in the SDK docs (text form):
----
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient.from_env()  # reads REDWOOD_API_KEY or prompts
print(client.whoami())
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-mini", prompt="Say hi in 3 words")
print(resp.text)
----
Notes: include equivalent Node snippet with import/await. Keep both under 15 lines.

Handoff templates to include in repo/docs (files to add under /examples/first-run/):
- 00-README.txt (one-liner + run steps)
- 01-python-minimal.py (example above with comments)
- 02-node-minimal.mjs (ES module example)
- 03-react-embed.md (tiny recipe showing how to call generate from a serverless function)
- 04-error-guides.md (mapping of common errors -> fixes)
- 05-telemetry-explain.md (what events we collect and why)

Checklist for SDK release cut (feature parity with docs):
- [ ] Add `whoami()` helper and friendly errors for auth failures.
- [ ] Add default retry/backoff policy and surface via `--verbose` logs.
- [ ] Include token cost estimation helper and expose `model_profile` metadata.
- [ ] Example code for streaming + function call in both languages.
- [ ] Instrument first-run telemetry events (first_install, first_success, first_error).
- [ ] Add README examples to NPM/PyPI package_homepage links.

Telemetry / Metrics to track for success:
- first_install -> package download + install events (approx from telemetry/analytics).
- first_run_start, first_success, first_error (with category).
- time_to_first_success (seconds).
- % of users who opt into telemetry.
- conversion funnel: install -> whoami success -> generate success -> go to examples page.

UX decisions / defaults to discuss:
- Default model for first-run: a small, fast open model vs a Redwood-curated low-cost host model. Tradeoffs: dev delight vs accuracy expectations.
- Should the SDK auto-upgrade telemetry schema? (probably yes with opt-out flag).
- If auth missing, offer `redwood login` (interactive) vs echoing env var instructions. CLI route is friendlier for beginners.

Edge cases / risk notes:
- First-run on on-prem/private deployments: can't reach hosted identity service. Plan: check env var `REDWOOD_PRIVATE=true` and run local handshake flow; provide a clear fallback doc.
- Corporate proxies and CAs can block package telemetry endpoints — allow telemetry to be disabled by env var and skip blocking during first-run.

Open questions (needs triage in sync):
- Q1: Do we require opt-in for telemetry, or is an initial opt-out prompt acceptable? (privacy/legal). Owner: @Claire.
- Q2: Should first-run include a tiny interactive web UI (sandbox) or keep everything in REPL/code? Owner: @Benji.
- Q3: Which model(s) are approved for use in the public examples without incurring partner licensing issues? Owner: @Diego.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Pair with infra to sketch `whoami()` contract and API behavior (Benji + infra).
- Draft the 01-python-minimal example and add to SDK repo (Aisha).
- Open a PR template for `examples/first-run` with the file skeletons (Claire).
- Sync with legal on telemetry wording and opt-in requirements.

Owners & tiny timeline:
- Aisha: examples + docs (2 sprints)
- Benji: whoami + CLI helpers (1 sprint)
- Claire: telemetry + legal review (1 sprint)
- Diego: model selection + cost guidance (1 sprint)

Notes to self:
- Keep examples tiny and copy-paste ready. Avoid advanced params in first-run that confuse.
- Add a short video GIF for README that shows 'install -> run -> success' for marketing page.

References / links to pull for final doc:
- CONFLUENCE: sdk-architecture/first-run (stub)
- JIRA: INF-987 (telemetry schema), INF-988 (whoami endpoint)
- Slack thread: #sdk-dx thread: "first-run ideas" (Feb 3 2025)

End of draft.

-- Aisha
